scenario.story: Coordinate your arrival with a teammate. Build one plan that satisfies every piece of the team’s evidence.
scenario.information: A game-inspired timing simulation using supplied rehearsal data. All times start from the same countdown. The final arrival must be within the tolerance and no later than the deadline.

tasks.title: Measure your travel time
tasks.intro: Four rehearsal runs take {{route_total}} seconds total. Each includes travel plus a {{reset}}-second reset. Isolate the travel time t.
hints: The parentheses describe one rehearsal: travel plus reset.
Divide both sides by four to find one rehearsal time.
Subtract the reset time from both sides.
tasks.takeaway: Grouping keeps repeated overhead attached to each run.

tasks.title: Predict your teammate’s arrival
tasks.intro: Three identical teammate runs and a one-time 6-second setup take {{teammate_total}} seconds. Find one run time a. The teammate begins at the shared countdown’s zero.
hints: Remove the one-time setup before dividing among the runs.
Divide by 3. That run time is the teammate’s arrival time from the shared zero.
tasks.takeaway: One-time overhead and per-run overhead produce different equations.

tasks.title: Recover the deadline
tasks.intro: Two equal arrival budgets and an 8-second reset take {{budget_total}} seconds. Find one budget b, the latest allowed arrival.
hints: The total contains two budgets and one reset.
Divide the remaining time by 2 to find b.
tasks.takeaway: A deadline becomes a constraint on the plan, not just a number.

tasks.title: Find every workable start time
tasks.intro: Use the team’s route, arrival, and deadline results. First find the starts s that give exactly the stated tolerance. Then find the full start interval within that tolerance, while meeting the deadline.
hints: Absolute value is the distance between the two arrival times. Two starts can be exactly 2 seconds apart.
After simplifying, open both paths: s − (a − 6) = 2 or s − (a − 6) = −2. Solve both.
The endpoints give a whole interval for “within.” Also require s + 6 ≤ b. The deadline may shorten the interval.
tasks.takeaway: “Exactly” gives boundary points. “Within” gives an interval. Every constraint must hold.

tasks.title: Two paths, a fresh equation
tasks.intro: Solve this new equation for every value of x. Isolate the absolute-value expression before opening its paths. Your check is saved separately.
hints: Undo the operations outside the absolute-value bars first.
Subtract 2, then divide both sides by 3.
Now |x − 4| = 3. Open the +3 and −3 paths and add 4 to each.
tasks.takeaway: Keeping both paths preserves the full solution set.
